goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:28 — The `h` value from `site_settings` is string-interpolated directly into a raw SQL `INSERT` statement, creating a SQL injection vector.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads `val` from the `site_settings` table, splits it into `records`, and then executes:

```rb
execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
```

Because `h` is interpolated directly inside single quotes with no escaping/quoting, a stored value containing a `'` (or crafted SQL) would break out of the string literal and alter the SQL statement. This is a real, verifiable SQL injection hazard in the migration (it should use connection quoting / parameterization, e.g. `quote(h)` or `exec_insert`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:14 — The `update` action does not check whether the lookup returned `nil` before passing the host to `save_host`, raising `NoMethodError`.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `save_host(host)`. If no record exists for the given `params[:id]`, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host` will execute `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil`. There is no guard or 404 handling in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:20 — The `destroy` action does not check whether the lookup returned `nil` before calling `host.destroy`, raising `NoMethodError`.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately calls `host.destroy`. If no record exists for the given `params[:id]`, `host` will be `nil` and `nil.destroy` will raise `NoMethodError`. The diff does not include any guard, `find` (which would raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`), or error handling to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:12 — The `update` action re-renders the serializer but never persists any changes, making the frontend `saveChanges` action a no-op.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, the action just `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without reading params or persisting anything. On the client side, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` (empty payload), so even if invoked it cannot cause any state change server-side. The only persistence for hosts is via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, making the embedding-level update endpoint effectively a no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb — There is no uniqueness validation on the `host` column, allowing duplicate embeddable host records to be created for the same domain.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `EmbeddableHost` ActiveRecord model with only a format validation (`validates_format_of :host`) and no `validates :host, uniqueness: ...`. The migration `create_embeddable_hosts` also does not add a unique index on `host`. As a result, the system can persist multiple rows for the same domain, and methods like `record_for_host` use `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (no deterministic ordering), so duplicates can lead to ambiguous/non-deterministic category selection and duplicated entries in the admin UI.
